stops.name: Jakobsbergs sjukhus
stops.story: Välkommen ombord på buss 953 mot Jakobsbergs sjukhus! Resan tar ungefär 16 minuter. Aspnässkolan, ett par minuter bort, var Järfälla sockens allra första egna skola och öppnade 1846 i en köpt mangårdsbyggnad som tidigare hade varit vägkrog. Det äldsta skolhuset revs 1959, men lever vidare på ett oväntat sätt: i dag fungerar det som vindskydd vid Ängsjö friluftsgård. Själva sjukhuset ägs av Region Stockholm och rymmer bland annat vårdcentral och apotek.

stops.story_en: Welcome aboard bus 953 towards Jakobsbergs sjukhus! The journey takes about 16 minutes. Aspnässkolan, a couple of minutes away, was the very first school of Järfälla parish, opening in 1846 in a purchased manor house that had previously been a roadside inn. The oldest school building was demolished in 1959, but lives on in an unexpected way: today it serves as a wind shelter at Ängsjö friluftsgård, an outdoor recreation centre. The hospital itself is owned by Region Stockholm and houses, among other things, a health centre and a pharmacy.

stops.name: Dackevägen
stops.story: Söderhöjden, en bit härifrån, byggdes 1967 som en del av miljonprogrammet, och här ligger Jakobsbergs bowlinghall. Torget rustades upp och invigdes på nytt den 31 augusti 2013. Mitt på torget står ett klotrunt konstverk som lyser i olika färger beroende på årstid.
stops.story_en: Söderhöjden, a little way from here, was built in 1967 as part of the Million Programme, and this is where Jakobsberg's bowling alley is. The square was renovated and reopened on 31 August 2013. In the middle of the square stands a spherical artwork that glows in different colours depending on the season.

stops.story_en: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Jakobsbergs sjukhus. Aspnässkolan, a couple of minutes away, was the very first school of Järfälla parish and opened in 1846 in a purchased manor house that had previously been a roadside tavern. The oldest school building was torn down in 1959, but it lives on in an unexpected way: today it serves as a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor recreation centre. The hospital itself is owned by Region Stockholm and houses, among other things, a health centre and a pharmacy. Thanks for riding with us!
